reference.title: Dumbbell Sumo Deadlift (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold the brace down and up, breathe out at the top.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, light touch, 1.3 s up

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbell; stop about 2 reps short of failure (RIR 2)
prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbell, then a kettlebell or barbell sumo deadlift

cues.text: Feet wide, toes turned out, one dumbbell hanging upright between the legs, both hands under the top plate.
Sit the hips back and down, knees pushing out over the toes, chest up, back flat.
Touch the end of the dumbbell lightly to the floor between your feet.
Push the floor apart and stand tall, the dumbbell rising straight up close to the body.
Squeeze the glutes at the top without leaning back; breathe and repeat.

mistakes.fix: Push the knees out in line with the toes all the way.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to reach the floor
mistakes.fix: Sit deeper with the hips or stop the dumbbell higher.
Keep it hanging straight under the shoulders.

kinematics.norm: More hip abduction and external rotation and less hip flexion than the conventional deadlift (Hanen 2025)
Quadriceps work more at deeper knee flexion; peak knee flexion did not differ from the conventional style (PubMed 11932579; Hanen 2025)
Feet wider than the shoulders, toes turned out about 30 degrees (clinical opinion)
More upright than a conventional deadlift (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #819212, Dumbbell Sumo Deadlift (male), video (movement reference)
An electromyographic analysis of sumo and conventional style deadlifts (Med Sci Sports Exerc 34(4):682-688, 2002; PubMed 11932579)
Hanen, Ben Mansour, Ertel, Duchene & Gauchard 2025, biomechanical analysis of conventional and sumo deadlift (Front Bioeng Biotechnol 13:1597209)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The dumbbell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Groin or hip pain: narrow the stance and turn the toes out less.
modify: Limited hip mobility: stop the dumbbell higher, or stand on two low steps.
Knee pain: sit back more and keep the shins more vertical.
regressions: Sumo box squat holding the dumbbell.
progressions: Sumo deadlift from a deficit (feet on two steps).

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hips as you stand; late in the lift it was more active in sumo than in the conventional deadlift (Hanen 2025).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Extends the hips as you stand; late in the lift it was more active in sumo than in the conventional deadlift (Hanen 2025).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Extend the knees: vastus medialis and lateralis were more active in the sumo than in the conventional deadlift (PubMed 11932579; Hanen 2025).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Extend the knees: vastus medialis and lateralis were more active in the sumo than in the conventional deadlift (PubMed 11932579; Hanen 2025).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: The wide stance puts adductor magnus to work as a hip extensor; it was more active late in the sumo lift (Hanen 2025).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: The wide stance puts adductor magnus to work as a hip extensor; it was more active late in the sumo lift (Hanen 2025).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Hip extensors; biceps femoris was more active in the conventional style (Hanen 2025).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Hip extensors; biceps femoris was more active in the conventional style (Hanen 2025).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the back flat; the sumo stance lets the trunk stay more upright (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the back flat; the sumo stance lets the trunk stay more upright (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the dumbbell by its top plate.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the dumbbell by its top plate.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders against the pull of the dumbbell.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders against the pull of the dumbbell.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Push the knees out over the toes.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Push the knees out over the toes.
